items.stem: The Horvitz–Thompson estimator of the population total is:
items.explanation: The Horvitz–Thompson estimator of the population total is Σᵢ∈s yᵢ/πᵢ, where πᵢ is the first-order inclusion probability. Each sampled unit is weighted by the inverse of its chance of selection.
Taking expectation over the sampling design gives E(Σᵢ∈s yᵢ/πᵢ)=Σᵢ yᵢ, so the Horvitz–Thompson estimator is design-unbiased for the population total, provided every πᵢ is positive.
The Yates–Grundy–Sen variance estimator is derived for fixed-size without-replacement sampling designs. Its pairwise inclusion-probability form uses the fixed sample size condition.
The Des Raj estimator uses the order in which units are selected in successive PPS without-replacement sampling. It is therefore an ordered estimator.

items.stem: In πPS sampling with sample size n, Σπᵢ over all N units equals:
items.explanation: In fixed-size πPS sampling, the sum of the first-order inclusion probabilities over all population units equals the expected sample size, which is n.

items.stem: The variance of the HT estimator is zero when:
items.explanation: If yᵢ is proportional to πᵢ, write yᵢ=cπᵢ. Then each sampled contribution yᵢ/πᵢ equals c, so the HT total estimate is nc for every sample of fixed size n; its design variance is zero.

items.stem: A well-known defect of the HT and YG variance estimators is that they:
items.explanation: The HT and Yates–Grundy–Sen unbiased variance estimators can take negative values for some samples/designs. An unbiased variance estimator need not be non-negative for every realised sample.

items.stem: The Hansen–Hurwitz estimator is used with:
items.explanation: The Hansen–Hurwitz estimator is used for sampling with replacement. It averages the observed yᵢ/pᵢ contributions, where pᵢ is the draw probability.

items.stem: Lahiri’s method is a technique for:
options: selecting a unit with probability proportional to size
items.explanation: Lahiri’s method is a rejection procedure for selecting a unit with probability proportional to size. It uses size measures and a suitable bound to generate the PPS selection.

options: the ordered version of Des Raj
the unordered version of Des Raj
items.explanation: Murthy’s estimator uses the unordered sample and averages over the possible selection orders. It is the unordered counterpart of the ordered Des Raj estimator.
